A.reason: M2 lacks a perfect fifth and carries a tritone directly above the tonic, so there is no stable consonance to rest on and no leading tone resolving it away - the ear is handed a fact it cannot resolve or renegotiate, only endure.

B.reason: M6 is the zero point of the whole set (raised-minus-lowered = 0) - every other scale here is defined only as a difference from it, which is exactly a system where identity comes from one's position inside a fixed order of differences.

C.reason: M7 differs from the stable M6 by exactly one raised degree, the sharp 4th, producing a scale that is almost the ordinary major but held up by a single idealized, slightly-too-bright note that keeps it from ever landing back on the ordinary.

D.reason: M4's step pattern (2-1-2-2-2-1-2 semitones) is a palindrome, identical read forward or backward, so the scale carries no built-in beginning or end, only a fixed recurring shape you are always somewhere inside of.

A.reason: At its worst the state doesn't turn into a different kind of sound, it just presses harder on the same one - M2 is already the limit case in this set (no fifth, tritone on the tonic), so there's nowhere further inside these seven for it to go.

B.reason: Pushed to its most oppressive, the order stops being a neutral reference point and becomes a closing wall - M1's b2 sits a half-step directly above the tonic, the tightest confinement of the tonic available in this set, which is what a rule feels like when felt only as constraint.

C.reason: At its most painful this state is not the shimmer of the ideal but the flat fact of having missed it - M3 is what M7 becomes with its one raised, aspirational degree removed and only the plain lowered 6th and 7th left, the idealized picture collapsed into ordinary loss.

D.reason: The pain here is that the cycle keeps being exactly itself no matter how much it hurts - M4's palindrome doesn't distort under pressure, which is the point; only the way it is played changes, not the shape itself.

unmatchable_reason: A, B and C are about how tones relate to one another at a single moment - resolved or not, hierarchical or not, idealized or not - which is exactly what a scale is. D is about the arrangement of moments across time, a periodicity of attention; a scale of pitches has no time built into it, so any match for D, including the palindrome I gave, is smuggling in a claim about rhythm or form under cover of pitch content rather than a principled fit of the kind A, B and C get.

A.reason: S3 has no perfect fifth and a tritone above the tonic together with the most heavily lowered profile in the set (raised-minus-lowered -5, including a doubly-diminished third and seventh), leaving no stable consonant frame to rest in - a sound that imposes itself rather than resolving.

B.reason: S2 is the most balanced member of the set (raised-minus-lowered -1, nearest to neutral) while still carrying both a stable fifth and an internal tritone, giving it a fixed frame plus a directional pull, the way a rule compels a specific resolution rather than merely existing.

C.reason: S5 is the most raised member of the set (+3), an inflated, reaching color that still keeps an unresolved tritone even with the fifth intact, so the brightness never fully settles - apt for an ideal image that is admired but never actually inhabited.

D.reason: S6's step pattern (1-3-1-2-1-3-1 semitones) is a palindrome, identical forward or backward, so the scale has no directional story of its own, only a position within a fixed, self-mirroring cycle - a structure organized by where you stand in a period rather than by where you are going.

recognised_family: the seven diatonic modes of the major scale (the church/Greek modal system)
source_of_part3: Both at once and I don't think they can be cleanly separated - the interval facts I actually cited (no fifth plus a tritone for M2, zero alteration for M6, one raised degree for M7, a palindromic step pattern for M4) are the very facts that gave these modes their conventional expressive reputations in film-scoring practice, so the convention is downstream of the structure, not a separate source I was drawing on instead of it.
